1.explanation: All of these skeleton components render a <label> element with htmlFor pointing to the input id but provide no text content (they rely on CSS skeleton styling alone). Without any descriptive text—either visible or via aria-label—screen readers cannot associate the label with meaningful instructions, violating DAP’s rule requiring descriptive label text. To fix the violation, each skeleton component’s label must include either placeholder text or a visually hidden descriptive string.
1.bug_scenario: The skeleton variants of form controls (Checkbox, NumberInput, Select, TextArea, TextInput) render only empty <label> elements (no visible or hidden text) for their placeholder state. When running the IBM DAP accessibility audit, each skeleton component’s <label> is flagged: “Provide descriptive text in LABEL elements. LABEL element is missing descriptive text that identifies the expected input.” The screenshots show each control with only a blank gray skeleton bar and an empty label, triggering the rule violation.

2.explanation: All of the skeleton components render a <label> with the appropriate ‘bx--…–skeleton’ CSS classes and htmlFor attribute but omit any text inside the label. Accessibility rules require that every label include descriptive text to identify its associated input. These Skeleton classes and function-components are responsible for the empty labels; they must be updated to supply either a visually hidden placeholder label or accept and render a prop for descriptive text, so that the DAP rule passes.
2.bug_scenario: When rendering the placeholder “skeleton” variants of form controls (Checkbox, NumberInput, Select, TextArea and TextInput), each component emits a <label> element with an htmlFor attribute but no inner text. DAP flags this as “Provide descriptive text in LABEL elements” because an empty label cannot convey what input it describes, even in a loading state.
